_README: Single source of the book's structure; the build is driven entirely by this file. Owl's Castle is a flat novel of 19 titled sections (no numbered chapters, no sub-sections), so each titled section is modelled as a top-level chapter (ch01..). Cite the book's own PRINTED FOLIO in notes, never the PDF page. NOTE the page-offset wrinkle recorded in source_note.
subtitle_en: A Novel of the Iga Ninja
rights: English translation and apparatus © 2026. Original work 梟の城 © the Estate of Shiba Ryōtarō.
source_ref: Shinchō Bunko edition, ISBN 978-4-10-115201-1 (¥890); the novel was first published by Kōdansha, September 1959 (Shōwa 34). Scanned by the Internet Archive, 2024 (fukuronoshiro0000ryot).
description: Shiba Ryōtarō's debut novel and winner of the 42nd Naoki Prize (1960). In the last years of the sixteenth century, with the country newly unified under Toyotomi Hideyoshi, an Iga ninja named Tsuzura Jūzō, whose family was slaughtered in Oda Nobunaga's invasion of the ninja province, is hired for one last impossible commission: to assassinate the ruler of Japan. His fellow disciple Kazama Gohei, who has abandoned the shadow arts to climb in the new order, is set against him. Through these two contrasted lives Shiba draws the ninja as he really was, a creature of shadow at the end of his age.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 梟の城 (Fukurō no shiro), Shiba Ryōtarō's first novel, made from an image-only scan of the Shinchō Bunko paperback with no digital text layer. The novel was serialised in 1958–59, published in book form by Kōdansha in September 1959, and won the 42nd Naoki Prize the following year. There is no prior published English translation of the novel; the title has reached English only through two film adaptations, released as Castle of Owls (1963) and Owls' Castle (1999). The present translation renders the title Owl's Castle.

The source is a vertical, right-to-left text set in the traditional way, with furigana reading-glosses printed beside the harder characters. The page images were recovered by optical character recognition tuned for vertical Japanese, and every proper name, number, and doubtful reading was checked against a magnified crop of the scan before it was translated. The scanned copy is missing the first of the book's two table-of-contents leaves, and its page numbering drifts by a leaf or two in the middle of the book; the section structure was rebuilt from the body itself and each opener's folio read directly off the page.

The apparatus is written for a reader with no Japanese and no background in the country's history. Footnotes supply the historical figures (Hideyoshi, Ishida Mitsunari, Tokugawa Ieyasu), the geography of Iga and Kōga and the capital, and the customs, offices and objects of the late sixteenth century that a Japanese reader would take for granted; the glossary fixes one English rendering per name. Where the scan is damaged or a reading is uncertain, the note says so rather than guessing.

Section titles are the author's own; several are evocative codenames or emblems (Water Dog, Carnage, The Paulownia Crest) rather than plain place-names, and are footnoted where the sense is not obvious in English.
source_note: Image-only PDF scan from the Internet Archive (fukuronoshiro0000ryot), 674 pages, no usable text layer (the Archive's own OCR misread the vertical Japanese as Latin and is unusable). Vertical, right-to-left; furigana throughout; all page furniture (running head 梟の城, folio) is at the TOP of the page, cropped away for OCR. The scan is MISSING the first table-of-contents leaf (the sections before 伊賀ノ山); the full section list was recovered from the second TOC leaf plus the body. PAGE-OFFSET WRINKLE: printed folio == PDF render page for folios 7-302 and again from 425 to the end, but drifts by +2 render pages across folios ~338-397 (an unnumbered leaf around folio 302-338, and an apparent 1-leaf scan gap around folio 397-425). READ folios off the scan in that middle span; do not compute. No embedded bookmarks.
